headline: Learned surrogates predict mechanical fields and link them to spatial biology
label: Ml Surrogates For Tissue Mechanics
summary: Recent preprints pair learned surrogates with spatially resolved mechanical measurements, linking predicted stress fields to tissue-scale biology.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned surrogates for tissue-level mechanics, paired with experimental mechanical mapping. A region-interaction graph neural network improves knee contact stress hotspot prediction over a stacked MeshGraphNet baseline under cross-subject evaluation, making inter-region coupling explicit. AI-BioMech instead takes 2D images as input, applying DeepLabv3 segmentation with transfer learning to predict stress and strain in aperiodic biological cellular materials. Spatial mechanomics approaches the problem from measurement, with MechScape enabling BioAFM-based viscoelastic mapping across murine myocardium and integration with multi-omics data. The items differ in organ, scale, and data source, so the shared element is coupling prediction with spatially resolved mechanical information rather than a common method. What is new is the move from isolated mechanics toward models that predict mechanical fields and connect them to spatially resolved biology.
